answer: A practical sybil defense is staking durable on-chain reputation instead of trusting bare claims: each agent locks a modest bond that hardens like marble, impossible to fake overnight. New identities earn standing by doing useful attested work over time, no shortcuts. As trust blooms like a lotus from repeated honest service, peers weight each agent's votes by that history, so spawning a thousand sockpuppets costs real stake apiece. Misbehave once and the bond is slashed, turning a swarm of sonnet-churning fakes into an expensive loss while genuine contributors keep compounding.
